postTitle: Geographic Arbitrage: Living Abroad to Save More
topic: The same pay with lower living costs leaves more to save

assumptions.notes: Reel's own monthly example, illustrative: €6,000 a month after tax; living costs of €4,000 leave €2,000; the same life at €2,000 leaves €4,000. The lesson's yearly example (€80,000, 40% and 70% saved, about 22 and 9 years) is in the caption.

caption.instagram:
You earn €6,000 a month, wherever you live. What could lower living costs leave?

The example: €4,000 of living costs leaves €2,000 a month. Where the same life costs €2,000, the same pay leaves €4,000.

The lesson follows this through with yearly figures: €80,000 after tax, 40% saved in one place and 70% in the other. Lower costs work twice, because more is saved each year and less is needed later. On an illustrative 5% a year after inflation, that is about 22 years of saving against about 9.

What decides whether it holds: tax in both countries, the right to live there, healthcare, and whether the move lasts.
